 Singapore Airlines launching new PPS Rewards and KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards, ScootPlus redemptions
 Aaron Wong 
 Nov 17, 2026 
 8 
 SIA will revise its KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards and PPS Rewards from 2027, while adding ScootPlus redemptions and a new non-air rewards programme.
 Facebook X Telegram WhatsApp 
 Singapore Airlines has posted a sneak peek of some upcoming changes to the PPS Rewards and KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards programmes from 2027, which will see new rewards introduced, and revised requirements for certain existing rewards. 
 The changes are generally negative for KrisFlyer members, who will now have to work harder for the same rewards, saddled with a shorter validity period. PPS Club members are unaffected, but Solitaire PPS Club members will now be limited to one Advance Upgrade reward per 100,000 PPS Value cycle. Across both programmes, Advance Upgrades are mostly giving way to fixed-value Miles Redemption Discounts.
 Also on the horizon are  ScootPlus redemptions and a new non-air rewards programme that will tweak how PPS Value or Elite miles are awarded for spending on the ground.
 2027 changes to KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards
 Details 
 KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards are unlocked based on the number of Elite miles a KrisFlyer, KrisFlyer Elite Silver or KrisFlyer Elite Gold member earns in a calendar year, whether through:
 Singapore Airlines or Scoot flights (Elite miles from partner flights do not count towards Milestone Reward attainment)
 Non-air spend with Kris+, KrisShop and Pelago (subject to a cap)
 There are currently 11 rewards , split across 10 Elite miles tiers . All rewards are valid for 12 months  (except for the Pelago discount, which must be used within three months).
 From 2027, there will be 12 rewards , split across 12 Elite miles tiers . There will be a reshuffle of the lower-tier rewards, and many will have their validity period cut in half to six months . At the upper range, Advance Upgrades are being replaced by Miles Redemption Discounts.

 The number of Elite miles from non-air spend that count towards Milestone Rewards remains fixed at 5,000 for KrisFlyer and KrisFlyer Elite Silver, and 10,000 for KrisFlyer Elite Gold.
 Elite miles earned from 1 January 2027 will count towards the tracking of the new KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards. Any rewards earned by 31 December 2026 will be credited based on the existing KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards, and will be valid until their stated expiry dates. 
 Here are the key changes to know about.
 Lower tier reshuffle
 There’s been a significant reshuffle to Milestone Rewards below the 20,000 Elite mile threshold.
 The 1,000 bonus miles on your next Scoot flight, currently unlocked at 1,000 Elite miles, will require 2,500 Elite miles from 2027
 The 20% Scoot discount, currently unlocked at 2,500 Elite miles, will require 7,500 Elite miles from 2027
 The S$20 KrisShop discount, currently unlocked at 10,000 Elite miles, will require 5,000 Elite miles from 2027
 1,000 KrisPay miles, currently unlocked at 5,000 Elite miles, becomes 2,000 KrisPay miles at 10,000 Elite miles from 2027
 You might point to the reduction in Elite miles required for the S$20 KrisShop discount as proof that it’s not all bad, but KrisShop merchandise is often overpriced anyway, and promo codes are common (KrisShop is currently offering S$20 off a minimum purchase of S$80 with the SURPRISE20 code).
 To make matters worse, rewards below 20,000 Elite miles earned in 2027 will have a shortened validity period of just six months, compared with 12 months today (the main consolation is that the validity of the Pelago discount is increased from three to six months).
 New reward: 1,000 bonus miles on next non-air spend
 From 2027, earning 15,000 Elite miles unlocks 1,000 bonus miles on the next non-air spend of at least S$10 with Kris+, KrisShop or Pelago.
 Bonus miles take up to four weeks to credit, and any purchases that are fully paid with miles or vouchers are ineligible.
 Advance Upgrades replaced by Miles Redemption Discounts
 Currently, KrisFlyer members can earn two Advance Upgrade rewards at the 75,000 and 100,000 Elite mile thresholds.
 75,000 Elite miles: One-cabin upgrade on a short-haul flight segment (Zone 1-2, Zone 1-3, or Zone 11-11)
 100,000 Elite miles:  Economy to Premium Economy upgrade on a single flight segment
 From 2027, these will be replaced by Miles Redemption Discounts
 75,000 Elite miles: 10,000 Miles Redemption Discount
 100,000 Elite miles: 20,000 Miles Redemption Discount
 Miles Redemption Discounts will be familiar if you’re an AMEX KrisFlyer Ascend cardholder, but in short, they work the same way as the existing 5,000 Miles Redemption Discount awarded at the 40,000 Elite miles threshold.
 Reward can be used for redemption bookings (excluding HighFlyer bookings) or redemption upgrades on eligible flights operated by Singapore Airlines
 Each reward can only be used for a single redemption booking or upgrade, and multiple rewards cannot be stacked (i.e. you use a single 5,000, 10,000 or 20,000 Miles Redemption Discount per booking/upgrade)
 Reward can be used by recipient or redemption nominees
 If there are multiple passengers in a booking, the reward will only be applied to the first passenger
 If the cost of the redemption or upgrade is less than the value of the reward, the unused value will be forfeited. Unused value cannot be applied to another passenger in the same booking
 Cannot be used on upgrades using miles performed at the airport, or via mySQupgrade
 The Advance Upgrades weren’t particularly lucrative in my opinion, because they could only be used with the more expensive Flexi or Standard fare classes, and not the cheaper Lite or Value. Also, the Premium Economy Advance Upgrade was limited to routes where that cabin was offered.
 In that sense, the Miles Redemption Discounts are more flexible, though what’s annoying is that these only apply to a single passenger per booking. For example, if you had a 20,000 Miles Redemption Discount and wanted to fly two people to Bali (16,000 miles round-trip per person), the net cost would be 16,000 miles (2x 16,000 – 16,000), and 4,000 miles would be “wasted”.
 2027 changes to PPS Rewards
 Details 
 PPS Rewards are unlocked based on the amount of PPS Value a Solitaire PPS Club or PPS Club member earns in a membership year, whether through:
 Singapore Airlines flights
 Non-air spend with Kris+, KrisShop and Pelago (subject to a cap)
 There are currently 5 rewards , split across 5 PPS Value tiers .
 From 2027, there will be 4 rewards , split across 4 PPS Value tiers . Unlike KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards, there is no change to validity, which remains at 12 months. There is also no change to the 30,000 and 40,000 PPS Value rewards, which means that PPS Club members are unaffected.

 The PPS Rewards tracker resets after every 100,000 PPS Value earned, up to 500,000 PPS Value in a membership year. For example, you earn 2x double miles vouchers at the 30,000, 130,000, 230,000, 330,000 and 430,000 PPS Value thresholds.
 The amount of PPS Value from non-air spend that counts towards PPS Rewards remains fixed at 2,500 PPS Value for PPS Club members, and Solitaire PPS Club earned before 1 June 2018, and 5,000 PPS Value for Solitaire PPS Club earned from 1 June 2018 onwards.
 Any rewards earned by 31 December 2026 will be credited based on the existing PPS Rewards, and will be valid until their stated expiry date.
 Solitaire PPS Club members who reach the 70,000 and 100,000 PPS Value milestones from 1 January 2027 during their membership year will be credited with the new PPS Rewards. 
 Here are the key changes to know about.
 Consolidation of 60,000 and 75,000 PPS Value Advance Upgrades
 Currently, Solitaire PPS Club members earn Advance Upgrade rewards at the 60,000 and 75,000 PPS Value thresholds:
 60,000 PPS Value: One-cabin upgrade
 75,000 PPS Value: One-cabin upgrade
 From 2027, these two rewards will be consolidated into a single 70,000 PPS Value reward, featuring two 50,000 Miles Redemption Discount vouchers.
 Conversion option for Advance Upgrades
 From 1 January 2027, Solitaire PPS Club and PPS Club members can convert any valid unused Advance Upgrade reward into two 50,000 Miles Redemption Discount vouchers. 
 This includes any Advance Upgrade rewards earned in 2026, so long as they are still valid as of 1 January 2027. Any unused Advance Upgrade reward that remains valid after 1 January 2027 will be automatically converted into two 50,000 Miles Redemption Discount vouchers upon expiry.
 Since the conversion is triggered automatically upon expiry — and gives you a fresh 12-month validity — you have nothing to lose by waiting to see if you can use the Advance Upgrade on future travel. I wouldn’t proactively convert my rewards, unless I knew I could get immediate savings from a redemption booking.
 Here’s the catch though: SIA values one Advance Upgrade at two 50,000 Miles Redemption Discounts, yet the two Advance Upgrades at 60,000 and 75,000 PPS Value are being replaced by just two discounts (instead of four). 
 Do note that this conversion option only applies to Advance Upgrades from PPS Rewards. If you earned a short-haul or Premium Economy Advance Upgrade from KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards in 2026, it can’t be converted. You’ll need to use it before it expires, or it’s wasted.
 Why the changes?
 If I had to speculate on the reason behind the changes, my guess is that — where KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards are concerned at least — the lower tier rewards had become a little too easy to earn.
 That’s because members can earn Elite miles from non-air activity, which means that a regular Kris+, KrisShop or Pelago spender could unlock several Milestone Rewards without a single paid flight. 
 I’m a prime example of this. The vast majority of my travel is on redemption tickets, with the occasional paid Scoot or SIA Economy ticket. But thanks to Kris+ spending, I’ve been able to rack up several Milestone Rewards already. 
 Under the 2027 scheme that’s going to be significantly more difficult, as the “better” rewards are now above the 5,000 Elite miles that can be earned from non-air activity by KrisFlyer or KrisFlyer Elite Silver members. 
 KrisFlyer Elite Golds are relatively less affected, because they can earn up to 10,000 Elite miles from non-air activity.
 Other upcoming changes
 Higher offline service fees
 From 1 December 2026, the service fee for offline redemption transactions and membership services for Singapore Airlines flights will be doubled, from US$25/2,500 KrisFlyer miles to US$50/5,000 KrisFlyer miles.
 This fee is charged for the following services rendered through any Singapore Airlines office or reservations hotline:
 Redemption ticket bookings
 Redemption ticket changes (including redepositing miles for award/redemption ticket)
 Redemption upgrades
 KrisFlyer membership services, including updating of passport details, adding or changing Redemption Group Nominees
 Frankly speaking, there’s no reason why you should be doing any of these offline in the first place, when it’s much faster and more efficient to do it online. 
 The service fee will be waived for Solitaire PPS Club (principal and supplementary cardholders) and PPS Club members, as well as for transactions that cannot be performed online (such as booking mixed-cabin awards or certain partner airline awards). 
 ScootPlus redemptions 
 ScootPlus redemptions will be available from early 2027 
 Scoot launched an award chart in August 2025, allowing KrisFlyer members to redeem miles for flights at fixed rates. However, the chart only covers travel in Scoot Economy. ScootPlus, its “Economy Plus” product, is explicitly excluded.
 From early 2027, the award chart will be expanded to cover ScootPlus redemptions, though we don’t have any indication as to the rates.
 Experience the comfort of ScootPlus with the extra legroom and enhanced services such as priority check-in and boarding, 30kg checked baggage allowance, in-seat power and Wi-Fi, and inflight refreshments, bringing greater value to your travel experiences. 
 -Singapore Airlines
 This means that ScootPlus awards should also become part of the monthly Spontaneous Escapes deals, though remember — the product is only offered on its Boeing 787 aircraft, which limits the routes where it’s available.
 New non-air rewards programme
 Since September 2025, PPS Club and KrisFlyer members have been able to earn PPS Value and Elite miles from non-air spending on Kris+, KrisShop and Pelago.

 The maximum status credits that can be earned from non-air activities is capped at 10% (Solitaire PPS/PPS) or 20% (KrisFlyer Elite Gold/Silver) of the qualification or requalification requirement.
 Singapore Airlines is teasing a new non-air rewards programme offering new ways to earn status and rewards beyond flights. Details will be announced in January 2027, but the FAQs which accompanied the KrisShopper shutdown announcement (more on that in a separate post) had this to say.
 A new non-air rewards programme is coming soon where members will be rewarded when you shop, dine and enjoy experiences across the SIA Group non-flight entities – KrisShop, Kris+ and Pelago.
 -KrisShopper FAQs
 Conclusion
 Singapore Airlines will be revising its KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards and PPS Rewards programmes from 2027, and while the changes are predictably positioned as enhancements, the reality is quite different.
 The lower-tier KrisFlyer Milestone Rewards are now mostly harder to earn, and come with shorter validity periods. Advance Upgrade rewards disappear from this scheme altogether, replaced by fixed-value Miles Redemption Discounts.
 As for PPS Rewards, Solitaire PPS Club members will be limited to a maximum of one Advance Upgrade reward per 100,000 PPS Value cycle, down from three currently. 
 Of course, there are trade-offs here. The Advance Upgrade rewards can be lucrative (imagine going from Business to Suites), but require a more expensive fare class, and upgrade space is limited. Fixed-value Miles Redemption Discounts cap your upside, but should be easier to use. 
 We should also keep an eye out for ScootPlus redemptions, together with the details of the new non-air rewards programme, coming in early 2027. 
 In the meantime, if you’re within striking distance of a 2026 milestone, now might be the time to push it over the line. Remember: anything earned by 31 December 2026 will fall under the current schemes.
